title: session-entropy-rebalancer-prototype-notebook
content:
Summary
---
Brain-dump: lightweight prototype for a Session Entropy Rebalancer (SER). Goal is to dynamically redistribute \"entropy\" (variance/uncertainty in context relevance) across active sessions to improve cache efficiency and reduce expensive cold prompts while keeping latency SLOs. This doc collects API shapes, config sketches, telemetry heuristics, rollout ideas and experiment plan.

Motivation
---
- We see tail cost where a small percent of sessions repeatedly trigger large model re-evaluations due to high context churn or unexpected instruction drift.
- Current prefix/KV caching is good but static TTLs and fixed prefetch windows are brittle across multi-tenant workloads and mixed short/long sessions.
- Hypothesis: actively measuring a per-session "entropy_score" and using a lightweight rebalancer to move prefetch, snapshot frequency, and caching aggressiveness will reduce token spend and lower tail latency.

Goals (non-exhaustive)
---
- Reduce p95/p99 token spend per session for top 5% most volatile sessions by >= 15%.
- Maintain p50 latency impact <= 3% and p95 impact <= 10%.
- Minimal operational surface: single new service + config API + opt-in per-tenant boolean.

Definitions / Mental model
---
- entropy_score: numeric 0..100, higher = more unpredictable context (topic shifts, instruction changes, tool calls). Derived from token-level surprisal estimates, instruction-change delta, tool-invoke rate, and recent model-change regressions.
- rebalancer: control-plane component that maps entropy_score -> action_set (snapshot cadence, prefetch window, quant profile, temporary pin to lower-cost model).

High level sketch
---
1) Real-time per-session signal aggregator (sharded at ingress): emits small vectors (session_id, entropy_score, recent_tool_count, last_instruction_change_ts) at 1s granularity.
2) SER decision engine (stateless, queryable): samples signals, computes smoothed entropy, outputs recommended action and confidence.
3) Action enforcer (per-runtime agent): applies local adjustments (increase snapshot frequency, expand prefix cache margin, throttle prefetch, route to canary model variant) and emits audit events.

ASCII diagram
---
[ingress] -> [signal-aggregator] -> (kafka/topic entropy-stream) -> [SER engine (query)] -> [enforcer agents on runtime nodes] -> [runtime apply changes]

API shapes (proposal)
---
1) Signal emission (lightweight): POST /v1/session_signals
{ session_id, ts_iso, entropy_estimate, tool_invocations_last_60s, instruction_delta_score }
- body size intentionally small; compressed protobuf later.

2) Decision query: GET /v1/rebalancer/recommendation?session_id=...
- response (simple map): { session_id, entropy_bucket, recommended_actions: ["snapshot:freq=30s","prefetch:lookahead=64","route:variant=fast-quant"], confidence_pct }
- important: actions are idempotent strings that runtime can parse; avoid nested objects for minimal rollout complexity.

3) Bulk push for control-plane changes: POST /v1/rebalancer/push_actions
- accepts list of session_id->action tuples, used for scheduled rebalances (not per-request).

Config sketch (notes for config service)
---
- entropy_bucket thresholds: [low:0-20, med:21-60, high:61-100]
- action map per bucket: set of strings. Example: 
  - low => ["snapshot:freq=300s","prefetch:lookahead=8","cache_ttl_multiplier=0.5"]
  - med => ["snapshot:freq=60s","prefetch:lookahead=32","cache_ttl_multiplier=1.0"]
  - high => ["snapshot:freq=15s","prefetch:lookahead=96","cache_ttl_multiplier=1.5","route:variant=stable-quant" ]
- per-tenant override and per-route override allowed.

Decision heuristics (early experiments)
---
- entropy_score = 0.5*norm_surprisal + 0.3*instr_delta_norm + 0.2*tool_density_norm (weights tunable)
- smooth with exponential decay (alpha=0.2 by default)
- cap snapshot rate to avoid IO storms (global token budget enforcement)

Telemetry / signals to monitor
---
- per-session: entropy_score_ts, recommended_action_ts, applied_action_ts, action_latency_ms
- outcome metrics: tokens_consumed_post_action_1m/5m, p50/p95 latency delta pre/post, model_switch_count, snapshot_write_bytes
- safety signals: increase in hallucination rate, user-facing errors, costly model fallback triggers

Enforcer responsibilities and constraints
---
- Must be best-effort; if enforcer agent fails, runtime should follow default aging behaviour (no action).
- Agents should confirm action idempotency and emit an audit event (session_id, action, before_state_hash, after_state_hash).
- For critical actions (model route change), require two-phase commit-ish acknowledgement: runtime pre-check -> apply -> confirm. For cheap actions (prefetch window, TTL multiplier) apply immediately.

Rollout plan (canary -> staged)
---
1) internal canary on test-tenant with synthetic churn workload. Observe token spend and latencies.
2) opt-in beta for 10 enterprise tenant groups (feature flag).
3) auto-rollback thresholds: >10% p95 latency regression or >5% increase in tokens for median sessions.

Experiment ideas
---
- A/B: baseline vs SER active where SER only modulates snapshot cadence. Measure token spend delta and snapshot IO.
- Multi-arm: allow SER to either (a) increase snapshot cadence or (b) route to lower-cost quant variant — measure quality regressions.
- Emergency mode: if downstream model capacity is low, SER should throttle prefetch aggressively (quick toggle).

Open questions / TODOs
---
- How to estimate token-level surprisal cheaply from streaming tokens without full forward pass? (approx via token-prob cache or small surrogate model). TODO: spike on surrogate estimator GH: redwood-inference/rebalancer#9
- Rate limits for signal emission and batching strategy.
- Clean semantics for action strings (define grammar) — avoid arbitrary strings in v1 if possible.
- Privacy: confirm no PII leaves runtime in any signal. Strip prompt bodies; only send hashed anchors.
- Reconciliation: what happens if enforcer applies an action but SER sees divergence? Build reconciliation loop.

Notes to self
---
- Start with a single action: snapshot:freq tuning. Lowest risk, measurable IO and token outcomes.
- Keep initial API minimal: signal POST + decision GET. Bulk push later.
- Add debug tracing flag to include session sample transcripts (redacted) for first 2 weeks of canary.

References / Links
---
- Related internal note: confluence://design/session-entropy-rebalancer-v0
- GH spikes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer/pull/7
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-1428 (experiment plan + dashboard)

Hand-off checklist (when ready for proto)
---
- [ ] spike: cheap surprisal estimator prototype (local microservice)
- [ ] minimal signal emitter in ingress shim (rate-limit + redact)
- [ ] SER decision engine stub (deterministic buckets, config-driven)
- [ ] runtime enforcer agent hook + audit event plumbing
- [ ] dashboard: tokens by session cohort, snapshot IO, latency delta

Random scribbles / heuristics tried earlier:
- treat tool_invocation as strong signal -> multiply entropy by 1.3 for 30s
- if routing variant changed < 5m ago, suppress further model-route recommendations for that session (cooldown)

End.

(Notes intentionally informal — will formalize into a PRD if prototype shows promise.)
